practices-58-1-4-abolition-of-zihar-divo.title: Abolition of Pre-Islamic Zihar Divorce ('Like My Mother's Back') and Expiation
practices-58-1-4-abolition-of-zihar-divo.note: Surah 58:1–4 addresses a woman disputing her husband's pre-Islamic zihar oath ('You are to me like my mother's back'), outlawing the Jahiliyyah divorce formula and mandating a three-tier expiation before marital resumption.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes recount that Khawlah bint Tha'labah complained to the Prophet after her husband Aws ibn al-Samit pronounced the pre-Islamic zihar oath, prompting revelation that replaced permanent separation with expiation.
discussion.reply: As al-Tabari documents on 58:2 from early authorities including Abu Qilabah, the formula 'You are to me like my mother's back' was a binding customary divorce oath in pre-Islamic Arabia. Rather than erasing the pagan oath's legal effect, Surah 58:3–4 recognizes the utterance as creating a binding marital prohibition that requires a tiered ritual expiation (kaffarah) to lift.

practices-58-1-4-abolition-of-zihar-divo.quranEn: [1] God has heard the words of the woman who disputes with you about her husband, and (who) complains to God, and God hears the discussion of the two of you. Surely God is hearing, seeing. [2] Those of you who declare their wives to be as their mothers’ backs – they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave them birth. Surely they indeed say a wrong word and a falsehood. Yet surely God is indeed pardoning (and) forgiving. [3] Those who declare their wives to be as their mothers’ backs, (and) then return to what they have said, (the penalty is) the setting free of a slave before the two of them touch each other. That is what you are admonished. God is aware of what you do. [4] Whoever does not find (the means to do that), (the penalty is) a fast for two months consecutively, before the two of them touch each other. And whoever is not able (to do that), (the penalty is) the feeding of sixty poor persons. That is so that you may believe in God and His messenger. Those are the limits (set by) God – and for the disbelievers (there will be) a painful punishment.

sources.title: Tafsir al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan)
sources.en: He, whose mention is exalted, says: Those who make their wives unlawful to themselves with God's prohibition upon them of the backs of their mothers, so they say to them: 'You are to us like the backs of our mothers', and that was the divorce of a man (from) his wife during the Jahiliyyah. Thus Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, he said: Zihar was a divorce during the Jahiliyyah, which if one of them spoke it, he could never return to his wife. So God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning it what He revealed.
highlights: 'You are to us like the backs of our mothers', and that was the divorce of a man (from) his wife during the Jahiliyyah
Zihar was a divorce during the Jahiliyyah, which if one of them spoke it, he could never return to his wife
sources.orig: يقول تعالى ذكره: الذين يحرّمون نساءهم على أنفسهم تحريم الله عليهم &; 23-228 &; ظهور أمهاتهم، فيقولون لهنّ: أنتن علينا كظهور أمهاتنا، وذلك كان طلاق الرجل امرأته في الجاهلية. كذلك حدثني يعقوب، قال: ثنا ابن علية، قال: ثنا أيوب، عن أبي قلابة، قال: كان الظهار طلاقا في الجاهلية، الذي إذا تكلم به أحدهم لم يرجع في امرأته أبدا، فأنـزل الله عزّ وجلّ فيه ما أنـزل.
